The Atlas Logistics pilot (March 1–April 30, 2026) met or exceeded every target in its measured results table. Against benchmarks, actual outcomes were: WAU 87.5% (target >75%), query success rate 84.2% (target >80%), citation accuracy 88.6% (target >85%, improved from 74% in March after the April 15 citation validation update), median onboarding duration 4.8 weeks (target 5.0 weeks), support escalation decline 18.4% (target >15%), and average query latency 1.8 seconds (target <2.0 seconds) [NL-020#NL-020-S04].

The pilot’s success was driven by pre-ingestion document cleanup (deduplicating, consolidating, and converting files), simple folder-based permissions, and direct frontline value such as rapid cold-chain alarm responses with page-level citations [NL-020#NL-020-S05]. Lessons learned include making document cleanup mandatory, keeping permissions simple for mid-market clients, and prioritizing mobile-friendly UI and messaging integrations for frontline staff [NL-020#NL-020-S07]. Friction points to address before expansion were ingestion queue delays and duplicate uploads (causing temporary citation errors), poor mobile usability on rugged warehouse devices, and missing analytical detail in InsightDash (e.g., exact queries and CSV exports) [NL-020#NL-020-S06].

The expansion recommendation is a phased company-wide rollout: Phase 1 (Q3 2026) grows active users from 80 to 500 across Chicago, Dallas, and Atlanta with a $2,500 onboarding fee and two training webinars; Phase 2 (August 2026) adds the advanced OCR ingestion pipeline; Phase 3 (Q4 2026) transitions Atlas to the Enterprise Plan (from $8,500/month) if adding delivery drivers pushes users past 2,000, with Microsoft Teams integration; Phase 4 (Q1 2027) establishes an automated API data pipeline and quarterly query-audit reports [NL-020#NL-020-S08].
